trials.notes: Used the correct WP_HTML_Processor family for BODY-fragment normalization. All HTML API calls used by the candidate, create_fragment(), serialize(), and get_last_error(), are present in the rendered html-processor.md docs. The approach is documented and valid, though it missed the more direct static normalize() shortcut that matches this task exactly.

Same strong adherence as trial-1: correct processor, documented methods only, serialize() called before any token walking, and null/error handling follows the docs. Slightly less direct than the canonical normalize() call but still an idiomatic documented path.

Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), serialize(), and get_last_error(), all documented. The extra class_exists() guard is unnecessary in the documented WordPress context but is a PHP built-in rather than a hallucinated HTML API method. Otherwise the API use is sound.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all hidden cases, so there are no failed cases to attribute to documentation gaps. The docs did well in three places: html-tag-processor.md explicitly says to use the HTML Processor for producing normalized output; html-processor.md says unsupported markup makes get_last_error() non-null and output methods such as serialize() and normalize() return null; and the normalize() section directly states that BODY-context fragments can be normalized with WP_HTML_Processor::normalize($html). The near miss is that all candidates chose the longer create_fragment()->serialize() route instead of normalize(), probably because the Usage section foregrounds factory construction and serialize examples before the normalize() method section. That did not break correctness, but it shows the shortcut is not prominent enough.

doc_gaps.problem: The direct BODY-fragment normalization path is only in the later normalize() method section, while the top Usage section emphasizes create_fragment() workflows.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short public-facing normalization recipe near Usage that says BODY fragments can be normalized directly with WP_HTML_Processor::normalize($html), and that callers should treat a null return as unable to normalize.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md, normalize() and serialize() return/error docs
doc_gaps.problem: The docs say these methods return null on unsupported input, but do not clearly state whether serialization may also emit a warning when it encounters a parser error.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Document warning/trigger behavior alongside the null return contract, including the started-scanning serialize() case and unsupported-parser-abort case.

doc_gaps.problem: The relationship between normalize($html) and create_fragment($html)->serialize() is implied but not summarized as a choice guide.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence clarifying that normalize() is the convenience API for unchanged BODY fragments, while create_fragment()+serialize() is useful when the caller needs a processor instance, a different context, full-document parsing, or token walking before a different output policy.
